record.paper_title: Periods of Integrals on Algebraic Manifolds: Summary of Main Results and Discussion of Open Problems
record.original_question: Does the global Torelli theorem hold for polarized K3 surfaces, that is, for simply connected polarized algebraic surfaces with trivial canonical bundle, so that the total polarized Hodge-theoretic period data uniquely determines the polarized algebraic surface?

evidence.quote: The global Torelli problem is the question of 'whether or not the total period matrix
(7.2). CONJECTURE***. The global Torelli theorem holds for K-3 surfaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ and $X'$ be two smooth complex projective K3 surfaces; that is, simply connected smooth projective surfaces over $\mathbb{C}$ with trivial canonical bundle $K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X$ and $K_{X'} \cong \mathcal{O}_{X'}$. Let $L \in \mathrm{Pic}(X)$ and $L' \in \mathrm{Pic}(X')$ be ample line bundles (polarizations) of the same degree. Consider the second integral cohomology lattices $H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$ and $H^2(X',\mathbb{Z})$, equipped with the cup-product intersection form (each isometric to the K3 lattice $-E_8(-1)^{\oplus 2} \oplus U^{\oplus 3}$), together with their Hodge decompositions
$$H^2(X,\mathbb{C}) = H^{2,0}(X) \oplus H^{1,1}(X) \oplus H^{0,2}(X),$$
and similarly for $X'$. Suppose there exists an isometry of lattices
$$\varphi : H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}) \longrightarrow H^2(X',\mathbb{Z})$$
such that $\varphi(c_1(L)) = c_1(L')$ and whose $\mathbb{C}$-linear extension sends $H^{2,0}(X)$ to $H^{2,0}(X')$ (equivalently, preserves the Hodge filtration).

Prove or disprove: there exists a unique isomorphism of algebraic varieties $f : X' \to X$ with $f^* L \cong L'$ such that $f^* = \varphi$ on $H^2$.

In other words, decide whether the polarized Hodge structure on $H^2$ together with the polarization class is a complete isomorphism invariant of polarized complex algebraic K3 surfaces (the global Torelli theorem for polarized K3 surfaces).
artifact.status_search_result: The global Torelli theorem for algebraic K3 surfaces was proved by Piatetski-Shapiro and Shafarevich (1971), with subsequent refinements and extensions (e.g., Burns–Rapoport, Friedman, Looijenga–Peters) including the case of Kähler K3 surfaces. The conjecture is therefore solved.

status_evidence.title: Piatetski-Shapiro–Shafarevich, A Torelli theorem for algebraic surfaces of type K3
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the global Torelli theorem for polarized algebraic K3 surfaces over the complex numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Global Torelli for polarized algebraic K3 surfaces was established in 1971.

status_evidence.title: Huybrechts, Lectures on K3 surfaces (Chapter 7: Global Torelli)
status_evidence.snippet: Statement and proof of the global Torelli theorem for K3 surfaces, attributing the algebraic case to Piatetski-Shapiro–Shafarevich and extensions by Burns–Rapoport and others.
status_evidence.claim: The global Torelli theorem for K3 surfaces is a theorem, not an open conjecture.
